newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals steady in narrow price range.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals steady in narrow price range.

text.p: Indian base metals on Wednesday were steady in a narrow price range on the local market, dealers said.
Demand from the industrial consumers remained sluggish but fewer arrivals of imported metals and a shortage of ready stock kept prices at previous levels.
"Inflows of imported metals from ports to the local markets remained low due to the ongoing strike of the transport operators," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
"Even deliveries of metals from market to industrial consumers were aLso affected due to the strike," he added.
In the ready delivery copper was steady at 13,550 rupees per quintal, zinc at 7,850 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees.
Sentiment for zinc however remained firm on the back of rising global prices and reports of a price hike by the state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd.
"Hindustan Zinc has hiked selling prices of zinc by 1,000 rupees per tonnes for April following sharp gains in the world market and a shortage of ready stock in the domestic markets," Parikh added.

On Tuesday Hindustan Copper also hiked selling prices of copper wire bar by 2,000 rupees per tonne while it lowered selling prices of copper rod by 1,000 rupees per tonne and kept prices of copper cathod unchanged.

Nickel was steady at the reduced level of 36,800 rupees per quintal after loosing 500 rupees last week, while tin was quiet at 31,600 rupees and aluminium at 7,450 rupees per quintal amid limited activity.
The undercurrent for aluminium was indicated firm on market talks that some of the major producers of aluminium in India are facing lower inventories of aluminium with them.
